subject: Possible inconsistency in PySTAN utility stan_rdump

messages.author: a7de39e424b27378
messages.subject: Possible inconsistency in PySTAN utility stan_rdump
parts:
SUMMARY of a possible issue:
Python implements arrays row-wise, Stan implements arrays column-wise.
This may have been overlooked in https://github.com/stan-dev/pystan/blob/develop/pystan/misc.py .
Direct usage of stan_rdump may lead to unexpected results.


DETAILED description:
Dear STAN community,

I wanted to share some debugging experience - maybe someone will have the same issue.

The data I am using in my STAN program is generated and used by a python script.
To convert python arrays to *.data.R, I am using the functions _dict_to_rdump, stan_rdump
from PyStan utilities (https://github.com/stan-dev/pystan/blob/develop/pystan/misc.py,
further referred to as [1]).

According to CmdStan Interface User's Guide 2.5.0, p. 70, data is stored in the column-major
order.

''... For example,

        y <- structure(c(1,2,3,4,5,6), .Dim = c(2,3))

This defines a 2 × 3 array. Data is stored in column-major order, meaning the values
for y will be as follows.

        y[1,1] = 1         y[1,2] = 3        y[1,3] = 5
        y[2,1] = 2         y[2,2] = 4        y[2,3] = 6
"

Using Python, I would define this array in the following way:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> y = np.asarray([[1,3,5], [2,4,6]])
>>> y
array([[1, 3, 5],
         [2, 4, 6]])

Assume that I want to put this array into *.data.R, so I copy the necessary functions from [1] and call

>>> data = dict( data_y = y )
>>> _dict_to_rdump(data)

As far as I can tell, this data is wrapped to *.data.R in [1, lines 969-971]:

"
     s = tmpl.format(name,
                            ', '.join(str(v) for v in value.flat),
                            ', '.join(str(v) for v in value.shape))
"

In our case, one can check that

>>> y.flat[0]
1
>>> y.flat[1]
3

etc., and

>>> y.shape
(2,3)

 i.e. the flattening of y happens row-wise. Thus, one obtains the following string dumped to *.data.R:

data_y <-
structure(c(1,3,5,2,4,6), .Dim = c(2,3))

That string will be unpacked by STAN in the column-major order, namely (cf. above)

        data_y[1,1] = 1         data_y[1,2] = 5        data_y[1,3] = 4
        data_y[2,1] = 3         data_y[2,2] = 2        data_y[2,3] = 6

which (IMHO) makes it very non-intuitive. I ended up exchanging "value.shape" in [1, line 971] by
'value.shape[::-1]", which leads to

data_y <-
structure(c(1,3,5,2,4,6), .Dim = c(3,2))

unpacked by STAN as

        data_y[1,1] = 1         data_y[1,2] = 2
        data_y[2,1] = 3         data_y[2,2] = 4
        data_y[3,1] = 5         data_y[3,2] = 6

which is not exactly the input array y, but it is the same as transpose(y). This, again, can be corrected
by using 'np.transpose(value)' instead of 'value' in _dict_to_rdump in [1], but I was not sure whether this
can lead to complications for high-dimensional arrays.

Best regards,
Arseniy.
